chunks: ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyād, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, from Diʿbil ibn ʿAlī, that he entered upon Abū al-Ḥasan al-Riḍā عليه السلام, and he ordered something for him. So he took it and did not praise Allah. He said:

So he said to him, “Why did you not praise Allah?” He said, “Then afterwards I entered upon Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, and he ordered something for me, so I said, ‘All praise is for Allah.’ So he said to me, ‘You have become disciplined.’”

key_terms.أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ: Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, the Imam who affirmed the learned etiquette
key_terms.اللَّهَ: Allah, the One deserving praise and gratitude
key_terms.الْحَمْدُ: praise; the expression of gratitude and acknowledgment of blessing
key_terms.تَأَدَّبْتَ: you have become disciplined; you have acquired proper etiquette and adab
key_terms.تَحْمَدِ: to praise; here, to verbally praise Allah upon receiving a favor

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith teach about praising Allah after receiving a blessing?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches the etiquette of thanking and praising Allah when receiving a favor. It also shows how the Imams عليهم السلام nurtured proper adab through correction and instruction, leading the person to learn gratitude in practice.
